note: GLOBALCIT's Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (EUI, 2025), coding the law in force on 1 January 2024 (A06a Const 27; A06b Const 27; L05 C1999 28.1): ordinary naturalisation after 15 years' residence; no renunciation of other citizenships required; a citizen keeps it on taking another (loss applies only to naturalised citizens, not modelled). Reforms after that date are checked in the file's later sources, where a later source is given. Citizenship at birth is read from the same dataset's 2024 coding of modes A01a (descent, born in country: Generally applicable provision), A01b (descent, born abroad: Generally applicable provision), A02a (birth in country: No provision) and A02b (birth in country to a parent born there: No provision), as its codebook (RSC/GLOBALCIT 2025/01, sections 3.2.1a to 3.2.2b) defines them: not by birth in the territory alone (provisions for foundlings and children otherwise stateless, modes A03a and A03b, aren't held by the form); by descent from either parent, with no further limit on a child born abroad. Changes to the law at birth after 1 January 2024 weren't checked for this file. On 2026-11-03 the primary was read: Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria 1999 (National Assembly download 5820), ss. 25(1), 27(2)(g) [the PDF's text layer drops the first characters of each line; dropped letters are shown in square brackets]; Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria 1999, s. 28(1)-(2). Every figure the file holds now rests on it, and the dataset is no longer cited. S. 28(2) makes a naturalisation conditional on renouncing within five months any other citizenship the person doesn't hold by birth; a citizenship held by birth is kept, so the file's renounce stays false. Loss on taking another (s. 28(1)) reaches only those not citizens by birth.

sources.title: Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria 1999 (National Assembly download 5820), ss. 25(1), 27(2)(g) [the PDF's text layer drops the first characters of each line; dropped letters are shown in square brackets]
sources.said: [ev]ery person born in Nigeria after the date of independence either of whose parents or any of whose grandparents is a citizen of Nigeria; and [ev]ery person born outside Nigeria either of whose parents is a citizen of Nigeria. ... [ha]s, immediately preceding the date of his application, either- [res]ided in Nigeria for a continuous period of fifteen years; or [re]sided in Nigeria continuously for a period of twelve months, and during the period of twenty years immediately preceding that period of twelve months ha[s resi]d[e]d in Nigeria for periods amounting in the aggregate to not less than fifteen years.

sources.title: Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria 1999, s. 28(1)-(2)
sources.said: Subject to the other provisions of this section, a person shall forfeit forthwith his Nigerian citizenship if, not being a citizen of Nigeria by birth, he acqui[res or ret]ains the citizenship or nationality of a country, other than Nigeria, of which he is not a citizen by birth. [A]ny registration of a person as a citizen of Nigeria or the grant of a certificate of naturalisation to a person who is a citizen of a country other than Nigeria a[t the ti]me of such registration or grant shall, if he is not a citizen by birth of that other country, be conditional upon effective renunciation of the citizenship or [natio]nality of that other country within a period of not more than five months from the date of such registration or grant.
